newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican labor boss Velazquez doing well -- doctor.
newsitem.headline: Mexican labor boss Velazquez doing well -- doctor.

text.p: Powerful Mexican labor boss Fidel Velazquez, 97, has been hospitalized with a urinary tract infection and is not as seriously ill as recent television reports have indicated, his doctor said on Friday.

For 60 years, Velazquez has been chief of the highly influential Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM), swinging vital labor support behind the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) and keeping a lid on labor unrest.
The frail labor chief has been in and out of the hospital regularly in recent months, but his doctor, Salomn Jasqui, said Velzquez is "doing well" since he was re-admitted on Thursday.

"After 24 hours in the hospital, he has improved quite a bit," Jasqui told Reuters. "He has a urinary infection, nothing more. He's eating. He spent the night well. He's a little weak, but there is nothing alarming."
The doctor could not say when Velzquez might be released from the hospital.
Velzquez, who has refused to step down despite his health difficulties, has no obvious successor.
Jasqui also denied television reports that Velzquez went 21 days without eating or sleeping during one recent hospital stay. "No one can go 21 days without eating or sleeping," he said.

Jasqui normally checks his patient into the private American British Cowdray (ABC) Hospital, but this time took him to the Presidential Guard Hospital, a military hospital, in order to keep out journalists, he said. Guards at the hospital entrance barred reporters from entering on Friday.
